name: Input
description: Input renders a labeled native input and extends its standard input properties with field layout, validation, and adornment options.

elements.name: label
elements.description: The label associated with the native input.

elements.name: type
elements.description: The native input type. Supported values include text, password, email, search, tel, and url.

elements.name: value / defaultValue
elements.description: Controls the input value or sets its initial value. Use value for a controlled input and defaultValue for an uncontrolled input.

elements.name: onValue
elements.description: Receives the current string value whenever the input changes.

elements.name: variant
elements.description: Sets the visual style to outlined (default) or underlined.

elements.name: size
elements.description: Sets the field size to sm, md (default), or lg.

elements.name: floatingLabel
elements.description: Places the label inside the field until it is focused or contains a value.

elements.name: labelPosition
elements.description: Places a non-floating label at the top (default) or left of the input.

elements.name: error
elements.description: Displays an error message, sets aria-invalid, and associates the message with the input through aria-describedby.

elements.name: iconLeft / iconRight
elements.description: Adds an SVG component or icon configuration as a left or right adornment.

elements.name: containerProps
elements.description: Passes native div properties to the field container.

elements.name: Native input properties
elements.description: Native properties such as placeholder, required, disabled, readOnly, pattern, and minLength are forwarded to the input.

accessibility.general: The component uses a native input and associates it with the supplied label using for/id. It preserves native keyboard, form, and validation behavior.
elements: Always provide a meaningful label; it is required by the component and remains available to assistive technologies.
Error messages are announced politely with aria-live="polite" and linked to the input with aria-describedby.
Use aria-invalid when an input is invalid without an error message, or use error when feedback should be displayed.
The read-only state adds a visual lock icon, but the native readOnly property remains the source of the input behavior.
